notes: Supplied primary title/DOI verified. PDF pages 9 and 10 rendered and visually inspected. Original side is an unassigned placeholder. No row mapping by audit ID, order, original-page sequence, or matching numeric values. Methods p. 2782 gives recruitment N = 273 and allocation n = 48 intervention, n = 56 no-intervention peer, n = 169 no-intervention non-peer; Table 1 p. 2785 repeats these group counts. These are not explicit final analytic counts for a specified critical model. Procedure p. 2783 reports one student withdrew from school mid-intervention. No analytic N sum performed and no N inferred from dfs. Printed F/t metrics retained as candidates without conversion. Canonical backslashes in p expressions represent <, verified visually in supplied PDF. Candidate tests on p. 2787/PDF 10: Behavioural-intention interaction F(3.58, 419.36) = 5.99, p < .001; condition F(2, 234) = 0.83, p = .44; time F(1.79, 419.36) = 2.28, p = .11. Between-condition post-test F(2, 259) = 3.20, p = .04; follow-up F(2, 245) = 1.43, p = .24. Intervention repeated measures F(1.48, 66.59) = 3.47, p = .05; no-intervention non-peer F(1.77, 249.77) = 11.77, p < .001; no-intervention peer F(1.71, 81.84) = 1.63, p = .20. Intervention pre/post t(46) = -2.31, p = .03, d = 0.28 with adjusted alpha .02; pre/follow-up t(45) = -1.26, p = .21; post/follow-up t(45) = 1.86, p = .07. Other non-peer paired contrasts and anonymous feedback n = 41 also appear; these are distinct tests/samples. Authors describe positive knowledge and attitude changes, marginal behavioural-intention improvement without maintenance, and variable spill-over. These are candidate narrative judgments; no unique row-specific verdict assigned.
